title: Build-versus-buy recommendation
prompt:
Write a recommendation of at most 180 words for the engineering director. Choose between
the two options using only the facts given, state the main risk of your choice, and say
what would change your mind.

Context: we need a job queue for sending about 2 million emails a day, with retries.
- Option A, managed queue service: $1,400 a month at our volume, 99.9% SLA, live in about
  one week. The vendor caps messages at 256 KB.
- Option B, run our own on the existing Postgres cluster: no new spend, about six weeks
  of one engineer to build and harden, and that team is already carrying on-call for two
  other systems.
- Our largest email payload is 40 KB. The launch date for the feature that needs this is
  in four weeks.
system:
You are completing one task from an evaluation suite. Do the task as asked.

Reply with the requested text only, with no preamble about what you are doing.

rubric.name: clear_choice
rubric.description: Makes one clear recommendation (A or B) instead of hedging or deferring the decision.

rubric.name: uses_facts_correctly
rubric.description: The reasoning rests on the given facts and gets them right: four-week launch versus one week and six weeks, the on-call load, 40 KB against the 256 KB cap, $1,400 a month. No invented facts or options.

rubric.name: risk
rubric.description: Names a real main risk of the chosen option.

rubric.name: reversal_condition
rubric.description: Says concretely what would change the recommendation.

rubric.name: length
rubric.description: At most 180 words and written for a director: direct, no filler.

reference:
Recommendation: Option A, the managed queue.

The launch is in four weeks. Option A is live in about one week; Option B needs about six
weeks of an engineer, so it would miss the date. Option B also adds a third on-call system
to a team already carrying two. The vendor's 256 KB message cap is not a constraint: our
largest payload is 40 KB.

The cost is $1,400 a month, roughly $16,800 a year, which is small next to six weeks of
engineering time plus the ongoing operational load.

Main risk: dependence on the vendor's pricing and its 99.9% SLA, which still allows about
43 minutes of downtime a month, so sends must be safe to retry.

What would change my mind: a launch date that moves out by two months or more, volume
growth that pushes the price up several times over, or payloads approaching the 256 KB cap.
answers:
Both options have their pros and cons and ultimately it depends on what the team values
most. Option A is faster but costs money, while Option B is free but takes longer. Many
companies start with a managed service and migrate later, although others have had great
success running queues on Postgres, and Kafka is also worth considering since it scales to
billions of messages. Given that our payloads can be as large as 400 KB, the vendor cap
could be a problem. I would suggest forming a small working group to evaluate all the
options in more depth and report back next quarter before committing either way.
